The CJMCU GUVA-S12SD UV Light Intensity Sensor Module is a compact analog sensor board designed to detect ultraviolet radiation from sunlight and other suitable UV sources. It uses a GUVA-S12SD gallium-nitride Schottky photodiode together with an onboard signal-conditioning circuit to produce an analog voltage corresponding to the detected ultraviolet intensity.
The sensor has an approximate spectral detection range of 240–370 nm, covering the UV-B range and most of the UV-A range. Its good visible-light rejection helps reduce interference from normal visible light, making it useful for ultraviolet monitoring applications.
The module has a simple three-pin interface consisting of VCC, GND and OUT. The OUT pin can be connected to the analog input of an Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi Pico, STM32 or another ADC-equipped microcontroller. The module can commonly operate from 3.3V or 5V systems, making it suitable for a wide range of electronics projects.
The analog output changes according to the detected UV intensity. A microcontroller program can process this output to create a UV monitoring system or estimate the UV index after suitable calibration.

The VL53L0X V1 is a compact Time-of-Flight laser-ranging sensor module designed for accurate, contactless distance and proximity measurement. Unlike conventional infrared sensors that estimate distance from reflected light intensity, the VL53L0X measures the travel time of an invisible infrared laser pulse, providing more consistent readings across objects with different colours and surface reflectivity.
The sensor incorporates STMicroelectronics FlightSense technology, a SPAD receiving array and a 940 nm invisible Class 1 VCSEL emitter. It can measure absolute distances up to approximately 2 metres under suitable operating conditions and communicates with microcontrollers through the I2C interface.
Its compact breakout-board design makes it suitable for Arduino, ESP32, ESP8266, Raspberry Pi, STM32 and other embedded development platforms. The module is ideal for robot obstacle detection, proximity sensing, gesture-controlled systems, object detection, automatic dispensing, smart automation, level monitoring and educational electronics projects.

• GPIO interrupt output
• Better consistency across different target colours and reflectivity
• Compact and lightweight breakout-board design
• Suitable for robotics, IoT, automation and DIY projects

The 7447 IC is a BCD-to-7-segment decoder and driver designed to convert a 4-bit Binary-Coded Decimal (BCD) input into the signals required to drive a common-anode 7-segment LED display.
It accepts a BCD number from 0 to 9 at its four input pins and automatically controls the seven display segments to show the corresponding decimal digit. This makes the 7447 useful in digital counters, clocks, scoreboards, frequency displays, digital meters, educational circuits and number display projects.

The 74266 IC is a digital logic IC containing four independent 2-input Exclusive-NOR (XNOR) gates. It is commonly used in digital logic circuits where two input signals need to be compared and the output must become active when both inputs are in the same logic state.
An XNOR gate produces a logic HIGH condition when its two inputs are equal, making the 74266 useful for digital comparison, equality detection, parity checking, control logic, binary matching and educational electronics experiments.
The 74266 belongs to the 74-series TTL logic family and is typically supplied in a 14-pin DIP package, making it suitable for breadboards, IC sockets and through-hole PCB designs.
A key feature of the 74266 is its open-collector output configuration. Because of this, an external pull-up resistor is normally required at the output for proper logic operation. Open-collector outputs also make the IC useful in certain wired-logic and interface applications.
It is suitable for students, hobbyists, technicians and electronics developers working with digital logic projects, truth-table experiments, comparator circuits, TTL circuits and embedded electronics interfaces.

The 1M Ohm Trimpot is a compact adjustable potentiometer designed for fine resistance adjustment, calibration, voltage setting, sensitivity control, and circuit tuning in electronic applications.
With a maximum resistance of approximately 1 Mega Ohm (1MΩ / 1,000,000 Ohms), this trimpot is suitable for circuits requiring high-value adjustable resistance. It is also commonly known as a 1M preset potentiometer, trimmer potentiometer, preset resistor, or variable resistor.
A typical trimpot has three terminals consisting of two ends of the internal resistive track and one adjustable wiper terminal. Turning the adjustment screw changes the position of the wiper along the resistive element, allowing the component to operate as either an adjustable resistor or a voltage divider depending on the circuit connection.
The compact through-hole PCB design makes the 1M trimpot suitable for electronic circuit boards, prototype PCBs, perfboards, control circuits, testing equipment, and DIY projects. A small screwdriver can be used to adjust the resistance during circuit setup or calibration.
The high 1MΩ resistance value is particularly useful for high-impedance circuits, sensor calibration, timer circuits, oscillator circuits, amplifier circuits, comparator circuits, threshold adjustment, reference-voltage adjustment, feedback networks, and signal-conditioning applications.
It can also be used in Arduino, ESP32, microcontroller, robotics, and IoT projects when an adjustable analog parameter or voltage-divider input is required.
Unlike a normal panel-mounted potentiometer that is designed for frequent adjustment by the user, a trimpot is generally intended for occasional calibration or internal circuit adjustment. Once the desired value has been set, it can remain in that position during normal operation.

The 1 Channel 5V Solid State Relay Module is a compact electronic switching module designed for controlling compatible AC electrical loads using a low-voltage control signal from Arduino, ESP32, Raspberry Pi, microcontrollers, PLC circuits, and other development boards.
Unlike conventional electromagnetic relays, a Solid State Relay (SSR) has no mechanical switching contacts. Switching is performed electronically, providing silent operation, fast response, reduced mechanical wear, and long operating life when used within the specified electrical ratings.
This module operates from a 5V DC supply and provides a single relay-control channel. It is suitable for projects where frequent switching, silent operation, and compact installation are required. Depending on the module version, an onboard indicator LED may provide visual confirmation of relay activation.
The control side can be connected to a compatible microcontroller digital output, allowing software-controlled switching of suitable AC loads. This makes the module useful for smart-home systems, automation projects, temperature controllers, lighting controllers, IoT systems, heater control, educational electronics, and prototype development.
Because a solid-state relay contains no moving mechanical contacts, it is especially useful in applications that require repeated ON/OFF switching. It also avoids the audible clicking sound normally produced by electromagnetic relay modules.
The screw terminals make load-side wiring convenient, while the control pins provide easy connection to Arduino and other controller boards.
Typical applications include AC lamp switching, heater control, home automation, IoT appliance control, temperature-based switching, timer systems, automatic lighting, industrial prototypes, and electronic control projects.
Important: Most commonly available 1-channel 5V SSR modules are intended for AC load switching only. The LM339 IC is a low-power quad differential comparator containing four independent voltage-comparator circuits in a single 14-pin package. Each comparator compares two input voltages and changes its output state according to which input voltage is higher.
It is commonly used in voltage-level detection, battery monitoring, threshold sensing, zero-crossing detection, waveform shaping, oscillator circuits, sensor interfaces and electronic control systems.
The LM339 can operate from a single DC supply or dual power supplies, making it suitable for many analog and mixed-signal circuits. Its input common-mode range includes ground when used with a single supply, which is helpful for low-voltage sensing applications.
Each comparator has an open-collector output. An external pull-up resistor is required to obtain a valid HIGH output level. This output arrangement also makes it possible to interface the comparator with different compatible logic voltages and combine outputs for wired-logic applications.
The standard LM339 supports a broad supply range and provides low current consumption. It is suitable for breadboards, IC sockets, prototype boards and through-hole PCB assembly.
How the Comparator Works
• When the voltage at the non-inverting input (+) is higher than the voltage at the inverting input (−), the open-collector output transistor turns off, and the external pull-up resistor produces a HIGH output.
• When the voltage at the inverting input (−) is higher, the output transistor turns on and pulls the output LOW.

The BC548 NPN transistor is a compact, general-purpose bipolar junction transistor designed for low-power switching, signal amplification and electronic control applications. It is widely used in DIY circuits, educational projects, audio preamplifiers, sensor circuits, LED controllers, relay driver stages and general electronic prototyping.
This transistor can be used as an electronic switch to control small loads from a low-current signal or as an amplifier for low-level analogue and audio signals. Its compact TO-92 through-hole package makes it easy to install on breadboards, prototype boards and printed circuit boards.
The BC548 supports a maximum collector-emitter voltage of approximately 30V, a continuous collector current of up to 100mA, and collector power dissipation of up to approximately 500mW, subject to operating and thermal conditions.
Different gain-group versions may be marked BC548A, BC548B or BC548C. These suffixes indicate different DC current-gain ranges. The exact gain and electrical characteristics may therefore vary according to the manufacturer and transistor marking.
Common Applications
• Small-signal amplification
• Low-current electronic switching
• LED switching circuits
• Buzzer driver circuits
• Sensor output circuits
• Audio preamplifier projects

• Signal-processing circuits
• Transistor-based logic circuits
Pin Configuration
For many BC548 transistors, when the flat face is held towards you and the pins point downward, the common pin order is:
Pin 1 – Collector
Pin 2 – Base
Pin 3 – Emitter
However, transistor pin arrangements can differ between manufacturers. Always verify the datasheet or test the component before connecting it to a circuit.

The LM386 Low Voltage Audio Power Amplifier IC is a compact mono audio amplifier designed for battery-powered and low-voltage electronic applications. It is commonly used to amplify small audio signals from microphones, radios, audio players and electronic circuits so they can drive a small speaker.
The LM386 has an internally configured voltage gain of 20, allowing basic amplifier circuits to be constructed using only a few external components. By connecting suitable resistor and capacitor components between pins 1 and 8, the gain can be adjusted up to 200.
Its low quiescent current and wide operating-voltage range make it suitable for portable speakers, mini radios, intercom systems, electronic toys, alarm circuits, voice amplifiers and educational audio projects. The IC can operate with speaker loads from approximately 4Ω to 32Ω, depending on the circuit configuration and supply voltage.
The common LM386N-1 version works from approximately 4V to 12V, while certain variants such as the LM386N-4 support higher supply voltages. Always confirm the IC suffix and circuit requirements before applying higher voltages.
The standard 8-pin DIP package is easy to use on breadboards, general-purpose PCBs and prototype boards. It is ideal for students, hobbyists, technicians and electronics developers building compact audio amplifier circuits.

The 7S 29.4V Lithium Battery Equalizer Board is designed for balancing the voltage of seven lithium-ion battery cells or cell groups connected in series. It is suitable for 7S 18650 lithium-ion and lithium-polymer battery packs with a nominal pack voltage of approximately 25.9V and a maximum fully charged voltage of 29.4V.
During battery charging, small voltage differences can develop between individual cells. This equalizer board helps maintain more consistent voltage across the seven series-connected cell groups, supporting better battery-pack performance and reducing cell imbalance.
It can be used in DIY rechargeable battery packs, electric bicycles, robotics projects, portable power systems, power tools, backup battery systems and other equipment operating with a 7S lithium battery configuration.
This is primarily a cell-balancing or equalizer board. A compatible BMS protection board may still be required for overcharge, over-discharge, overcurrent and short-circuit protection.
Important: Connect the balance wires in the correct sequence, starting from the battery pack negative terminal. Incorrect wiring may damage the board or battery cells. Use cells of the same chemistry, capacity, voltage and condition.

The 6–30V 1-Channel Power Relay Module with Adjustable Timing Cycle is a self-contained timer-controlled switching solution widely used in electronics education, automation prototyping, and control system demonstrations. Unlike programmable boards that require firmware development, this module offers direct hardware-based timing control through onboard buttons and a digital display.
It is designed to simplify time-based switching tasks such as delayed start, delayed stop, cyclic operation, and signal-controlled holding. The wide voltage input range and simple trigger interface allow it to integrate easily with microcontrollers, PLC outputs, sensors, and manual switches.
Q&A
Q: Is this a programmable board like Arduino?
A: No. This is a hardware timer relay module that works without coding.
Technical Architecture
At its core, the module consists of a timing control circuit, a microcontroller-based timing logic unit, a seven-segment LED display, and a single electromechanical relay. An optocoupler is used on the trigger input side to electrically isolate the control signal from the relay output.
The relay contacts act as a passive switch, allowing the module to control external loads without sharing power between control and load circuits. Timing parameters are stored in non-volatile memory, ensuring settings are retained even after power loss.
Problem–Solution
Problem: Microcontroller GPIO pins cannot directly switch high-voltage loads.
Solution: This relay module provides electrical isolation and safe switching.
Why Choose This Model?
This model is chosen frequently because it combines wide voltage support, flexible timing modes, and standalone operation. Users do not need programming knowledge or external displays to configure delays.
Key advantages
• Wide 6–30V operating range
• Adjustable timing from milliseconds to hours
• Clear LED display for configuration feedback
• Emergency STOP function for safety
Comparison
Compared to simple relay modules, this timer relay provides built-in timing logic. Compared to PLC timers, it is compact and cost-effective. Compared to microcontroller-based solutions, it eliminates firmware complexity.

A drone kit typically includes the necessary components to assemble and operate a drone, whether for hobby, educational, or professional purposes.

• Frame:
• The body or structure of the drone.
• Materials: Carbon fiber, plastic, or aluminum (lightweight and durable).
• Motors:
• Usually brushless DC motors for longer lifespan and efficiency.
• 4 motors for quadcopters, more for advanced configurations.
• Electronic Speed Controllers (ESCs):
• Regulates the speed of the motors.
• Ensures smooth operation and control.
• Propellers:
• Two types: Clockwise (CW) and Counterclockwise (CCW).
• Material: Plastic or carbon fiber.
• Flight Controller:
• The "brain" of the drone, controls stability and movement.
• Popular models: Pixhawk, KK, APM, Naze32.
• Battery and Charger:
• Typically a LiPo (Lithium Polymer) battery.
• Voltage and capacity depend on the drone's size and power requirements.
• Radio Transmitter and Receiver:
• For wireless control.
• Common configurations: 6-channel or more.
• GPS Module (Optional):
• For navigation and advanced features like Return to Home (RTH).
• Camera and Gimbal (Optional):
• For aerial photography or FPV (First Person View).
• Gimbal stabilizes the camera during flight.
• FPV System (Optional):
• Includes an FPV camera and video transmitter.
• Displays a live video feed to goggles or a screen.
• Power Distribution Board (PDB):
• Distributes power from the battery to the motors and ESCs

• Measuring Range: 20 cm to 450 cm (typical up to 4.5 meters)
• Blind Zone: 20 cm (minimum detection distance)
• Operating Voltage: 5V DC
• Operating Current: 15–30 mA (typical)

• Output Signal: Digital TTL Pulse (Trigger/Echo)
• Interface Pins:
• VCC
• GND

• ECHO
